Rufus
ROO-fus
proper noun
Latin Rufus, “red” or “red-haired,” a believer at Rome chosen in the Lord, likely the son of Simon of Cyrene.

See also: Rufus

📖 Biblical Definition

Rufus is named in the greetings of Romans: “Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine” (Rom 16:13). He is very likely the same Rufus named in the Gospel of Mark, where Simon of Cyrene, compelled to bear the cross of Christ, is called “the father of Alexander and Rufus” (Mar 15:21) — a notice that would have meaning only if his sons were known to the church for whom Mark wrote. If so, Rufus was the son of the man who carried the Saviour’s cross to Golgotha, and the blessing that fell upon that house through so solemn an errand is a marvel of providence. Paul calls him “chosen in the Lord,” a phrase that breathes the sovereign electing grace of God, for the saints are chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:4). And with tender affection he greets the mother of Rufus as “his mother and mine,” testifying that this godly woman had shown Paul such motherly kindness that he counted her his own mother in the faith. Rufus stands as a witness to the riches of electing grace, that the Lord marks out His own; and to the sweetness of the communion of saints, in which a brother is chosen in the Lord and a sister becomes a mother to a stranger for Christ’s sake.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A believer at Rome “chosen in the Lord,” likely the son of Simon of Cyrene who bore the cross (Rom 16:13).

expand to see more

RUFUS, a believer at Rome, “chosen in the Lord” (Rom 16:13).

Paul greets his mother as “his mother and mine.”

He is likely the son of Simon of Cyrene (Mar 15:21).

His father bore the cross of Christ to Golgotha.

His name signifies “red” or “red-haired.”

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 16:13 — "Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine."

Mar 15:21 — "And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross."

Eph 1:4 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

1Th 1:4 — "Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A saint of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to electing grace and the tenderness of the communion of saints.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the riches of electing grace and the tenderness of the communion of saints. Paul calls Rufus “chosen in the Lord,” a phrase that breathes God’s sovereign election, for the saints are chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world. To be marked out as the Lord’s own is the deepest ground of a believer’s comfort, and the apostle delights to name a humble brother by that high title.

The greeting of Rufus’s mother as “his mother and mine” also witnesses to the sweetness of the household of faith, in which a godly woman becomes a mother to a stranger for Christ’s sake. And if, as is likely, Rufus was the son of Simon of Cyrene who bore the Saviour’s cross, his house shows the marvel of providence, by which a solemn errand laid upon a passing stranger became the door of blessing to his children and his children’s house.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “red” or “red-haired,” borne by a believer chosen in the Lord.

"Like Rufus, the saints are “chosen in the Lord,” marked out by God’s sovereign electing grace."

"Rufus teaches the sweetness of the household of faith, where a sister becomes a mother for Christ’s sake."

"His likely descent from Simon of Cyrene shows providence turning a hard errand into a door of blessing."
